title: Identify milling and reclaiming safety procedures
intro: A milling plan must account for the cutting system, material discharge, truck movement, traffic and people on the ground. Agree on boundaries and communication before the rotor or travel system moves.

sections.title: Interpret and follow job plan
sections.text: Read the path, pattern, depth, pass sequence, utilities, obstacles, discharge arrangement and planned stopping points. Confirm the current revision and who can authorize a change. Walk the area only when access is controlled. Resolve utility information and unidentified obstructions before cutting. Brief the plan with ground crew, truck drivers and traffic-control personnel, using a drawing and read-back.

sections.title: Demonstrate awareness of machine-specific safety
sections.text: Recognize rotor and conveyor entanglement, ejected material, silica-containing dust, exhaust, noise, hot surfaces, pressurized hydraulics, blind areas and raised components. Dust control is an engineered system requiring inspection and effective operation; a visible spray does not prove adequate exposure control. Block or support raised equipment using specified devices before access. Guard removal, clearing jams and service require the applicable isolation procedure.

sections.title: Describe Traffic Control requirements
sections.text: The traffic-control plan and site assessment determine TCP positions, numbers, signs, devices and communication. Milling traffic, public traffic and pedestrians can change relative positions as work advances. Keep a defined route and reassess driveways, intersections and service access. Only trained and authorized people perform assigned traffic-control roles. Stop if control or communication is lost.

sections.title: Describe proper PPE
sections.text: Select PPE through the hazard assessment and current requirements, including suitable footwear, head, eye, hearing and high-visibility protection as applicable. Respiratory protection requires the employer’s program, correct selection, training and fit testing where required. WorkSafeBC Part 8 assigns workers specified basic clothing, general-purpose gloves, footwear and safety headgear, while employers provide other required PPE; agreements may provide more. The employer must ensure required PPE is used and maintained.

sections.title: Describe lockout procedures
sections.text: Identify every hazardous energy source, including engine/fuel, electrical, hydraulic, gravity, rotating parts and stored pressure. Use the machine-specific written lockout procedure: stop, isolate, secure, dissipate or restrain stored energy and verify the safe state before work. A key removed or battery switch off does not alone establish full isolation. Each worker’s protection follows the applicable lockout system.

sections.title: Describe how to secure equipment for safety
sections.text: Park in the designated stable location, lower or support components as instructed, apply parking controls and required chocks, and secure keys and access. Protect the public from the machine and residual hazards. Remove or secure detachable items without leaving guards missing. Record defects and communicate the machine’s status to the next shift.

worked.title: A changed discharge route
worked.case: The planned truck position is blocked by a delivery vehicle. Someone proposes swinging the conveyor over a pedestrian route.
worked.solution: Stop the conflicting movements, preserve the pedestrian boundary and ask the lead to revise the arrangement with traffic control. Check overhead and swept-path hazards. Resume only after the new plan is communicated and controls are in place.

activities.prompt: Name four hazardous energies that can remain after engine shutdown.
activities.answer: Gravity in raised components, hydraulic pressure, rotating inertia and electrical/stored energy may remain. The actual machine assessment determines all sources and controls.
activities.title: Name four hazardous energies that can remain after engine shutdown.

activities.prompt: Write a read-back for a revised milling boundary at station 0+120.
activities.answer: State station, lane/side, revised limit, discharge route, protected public route, stop signal and person authorizing the change. Ask the lead to confirm the interpretation.
activities.title: Write a read-back for a revised milling boundary at station 0+120.

activities.prompt: A dust-control alarm appears while cutting. What evidence should be retained?
activities.answer: Record machine, time, station, alarm and observed conditions; stop or hold as required by the safe procedure and notify the lead. Preserve the fault and correction record before authorized resumption.
activities.title: A dust-control alarm appears while cutting

practical: Brief and verify the work-zone boundary.
Demonstrate the approved lockout with all energy sources controlled.
Secure the parked machine and communicate its status.
